chapter: Road bands: Hucklebuck Williams and Tiny Bradshaw
title: The bus fire on New Year's morning near Tuskegee
summary: The band bus burns on the way to a Tuskegee homecoming; Sam saves his bass while the horns and clothes are lost and the school helps out.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: And stayed with the band until we had a tragedy. You know, it wasn't tragic, but it was, you know, an accident with the bus on the--on ah--on New Year's morning. We was going to Tusc--ah, Alabama. We was on the road and the bus caught on fire.

Everybody was sleeping. So the bus driver--the guy's name was Nick. So I was standing--everybody was asleep but me. I was, you know, I was--so I was standing down in the well. You know that little well, you know--

So I'm standing down there talking to Nick, you know, keep trying to keep him company, you know, cause everybody's asleep. We--we doing these one-nighters so we was going to this Alabama. What's the name of that big university down there in Alabama where all those flowers come from.
Tuskegee. You know that big homecoming
football game. We...supposed to play there.

So we just--so Nick was hitting it too. He was rolling. And so I was sitting down there talking to him, keeping him company. And so, after a while, a car came by and got right on the side of the bus and blew--blowing the horns. "Beep--beep--beep." Say "your bus is on fire in the back!" So we pulled the bus over and got out, man. And went in the back of the bus with a flashlight. And we looked all up under the thing and lifted the thing and looked all in the motor. Didn't see nothing.
So we got back in the bus, man, and we was hitting it. And I started smelling something that smelled like rubber.
Then another car came by, said--blowed the horn said "man, you bus is on fire!" And that time, we pulled it over, man. The whole rear end was like in flames, you know.
So I ran in the bus there, man. Started waking the guys up.
And it--it was cold, too, you know. That's New Year's morning.
Lot of those guys--we had everything on that bus, you know. Lot of those guys just go to bed and shoes and stuff off. They would all cover up.
With their pillows and stuff--asleep, you know, with shoes off. And by the time that bus stopped, and I kept waking guys up getting them out of there--
That bus was in full flame, man.

Just burning. And just standing out there looking at it, man, I thought about it and I had a hell of a bass, man. And I thought about that bass, man, in that bus. And I went in there and got my bass, man.
I went in there and by the time I got my bass and got out and ran across the field, one of them gas tanks went. And we had two gas--
And one of them boys went, man. Went BOOM. And, and, and, and, and all those clothes--instruments--music--everything, man. And we standing out there looking at it going up in flames, man.
Paul was standing looking at all that money go up in flames. Everything. Guys didn't have no shoes on, man.
Standing out there and it was cold, man.
And Lee Polk hurt his back getting out of that bus. He snapped something back there.
And he, he never, never got straight after that either. So I left that band.
Well you saved your bass, though.
I got my bass out of there. I got my bass.
Stood--standing in this cornfield with that fellow. I was the only guy there that had his own, you know, his instrument, man.
So, they had to send cabs out there. In fact, we was--you know, we were--we were like on the outskirts of town.

Little bit more, we would have made it right in town. We was on the outskirts of town, man. They sent cabs and stuff out there for us. Took us in, you know. And the people from their school, man, they all took up collection. And all those guys that didn't have clothes and shoes--
And gave 'em instruments to play for that night.
I was cool. I had my--I had my stuff.
I had my fiddle, you know. Didn't have to give me no fiddle. I got mine.
